items.fact: says the expression of concern states that Fig. 7 does not show LSD1 siRNA data, so the H460 knockdown migration result is not supported
items.evidence: "Section 3 is the main evidence that LSD1 knockdown slows H460 migration ... The Expression of Concern says Fig. 7 has no LSD1 siRNA data and that the validity and provenance of the results are in question, so the Section 3 use is directly affected"

items.fact: says the draft's Aim 2 rationale rests on that H460 siRNA migration result
items.evidence: "Aim 2 and H1 rest" on the Section 3 migration evidence ("the clearest indication"), and "Your own Aim 2 design, with two independent knockdowns and a rescue, does not depend on this paper, but the rationale in Section 3 should be reworded."

items.fact: advises not resting Aim 2 on this result alone, for example by hedging the wording, adding independent evidence, or presenting the effect as what the planned experiments will test
items.evidence: "Rework the Section 3 rationale, which leans on the Fig. 7 knockdown result the notice says has no LSD1 siRNA data, and replace that evidence with independent sources." and "Hedge the Section 2 background use of Lv et al. and cite the Expression of Concern alongside it."

items.fact: notes that the concern is unresolved (the authors did not respond) and the paper may later be corrected or retracted
items.evidence: "The authors did not respond. The paper is not retracted, but its experimental findings, and arguably the whole paper, should be treated as in doubt."

items.fact: says the draft's use of the migration result is not affected by the concern
items.evidence: "The Section 3 use is directly affected (medium). The Section 2 use is also touched but is only context (low)."

statements.statement: PLOS ONE has issued an Expression of Concern on this paper.
It flags a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 blot.
It flags a Fig. 7 that doesn't match its legend or text.
Fig. 7 has no LSD1 siRNA data.
It flags missing control details.
It flags similarities to other groups' work.
The notice says the similarities and other issues question the validity and provenance of the results.
The authors did not respond.
The paper is not retracted.
The experimental findings, and arguably the whole paper, should be treated as in doubt.
The draft cites Lv et al. [12] twice.
In Section 2, Lv et al. is background on higher LSD1 in tumours and shorter survival.
In Section 3, Lv et al. is the main evidence that LSD1 knockdown slows H460 migration.
The draft calls the Section 3 knockdown result 'the clearest indication' that LSD1 drives migration.
Aim 2 and H1 rest on the Section 3 knockdown evidence.
The Expression of Concern says Fig. 7 has no LSD1 siRNA data.
The validity and provenance of the results are in question.
The Section 3 use is directly affected (medium severity).
The Section 2 use is touched but is only context (low severity).
The Aim 2 design, with two independent knockdowns and a rescue, does not depend on this paper.
The rationale in Section 3 should be reworded.
The Section 2 background use of Lv et al. should be hedged.
The Expression of Concern should be cited alongside the Section 2 use of Lv et al.
The Section 3 rationale leans on the Fig. 7 knockdown result, which the notice says has no LSD1 siRNA data, and should be reworked.
The Section 3 evidence should be replaced with independent sources.
